briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. Welcome to the climate briefing for August 20, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis, Expanding Global Impact
sections.content: According to news collected today, major global cities are experiencing increasing damage due to climate change, with damage particularly projected to concentrate in Seoul, South Korea [2]. Globally, marine heatwaves are a serious concern, with sea temperatures in Europe and South Korea rising by 6℃, and research findings also published indicating marine heatwaves observed in Europe [10, 115]. Domestically, heatwaves of 42.5 degrees Celsius have occurred or could occur on the Korean Peninsula, with warnings of potential 50-degree heatwaves, alongside extreme weather phenomena such as 'extreme droughts and extreme torrential rains' [13, 18, 33]. Internationally, the UK experienced its hottest, driest, and deadliest summer on record with no rain for 61 days, resulting in approximately 3,000 deaths, and most of England and Wales are in drought conditions, directly impacted by climate change [131, 132, 134]. Furthermore, climate change is causing changes in diarrhea prevalence in several African countries, and in the Arctic, the disappearance of ice is leading to 'feeding frenzies' among large whales, severely impacting ecosystems [114, 121, 128].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Adaptation Efforts to Combat Climate Change
sections.content: Adaptation efforts in the agricultural sector to respond to climate change are active. Young farmers from Daejeon explored agricultural solutions and management strategies for climate change in Jeju, conducting field visits related to subtropical crops and abnormal weather conditions [3, 7, 8, 16, 17, 21, 23, 27, 30, 31]. In Europe, interest in heat-resistant agricultural technologies is growing, leading to increased investment from companies like McDonald's and Nestlé, while domestically, Seosan City and Hampyeong County are preparing for abnormal weather through potato and grape cultivation technology training [6, 12, 14, 29]. As part of these adaptation efforts, the K-agriculture digital platform 'WISE,' jointly developed by South Korea and the United States, was launched globally on a UN platform, predicting droughts and floods in farmlands worldwide [24, 26, 28, 34]. Additionally, citizen scientists are collecting 400,000 pieces of bio-information to address climate change and invasive species, and the Northern Regional Forest Service is identifying excellent afforestation sites for climate change response, demonstrating multifaceted efforts [15, 19].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Activities and Policies for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts for achieving carbon neutrality are underway in both the private and public sectors. CATL has become the first TWh-class shipping company to achieve carbon neutrality at its core operational sites and is pursuing 'zero-carbon' battery production through an AI factory powered 100% by solar energy [35, 41, 72, 75]. At the local government level, Ansan City's Carbon Neutrality Support Center is promoting 'Carbon Neutrality Leading Projects,' and 40 daycare centers in Daejeon Jung-gu and Sejong City are encouraging eco-friendly practices in daily life, such as the '1.5℃ Carbon Neutrality Challenge' and resource circulation campaigns [36, 38, 39, 52, 54, 71]. The Yongin Special City Council launched 'Carbon Neutrality Research Institute IV' and commenced research on circular economy-based carbon neutrality policies, with the government establishing 5-year support plans for the carbon-neutral transition of the Hanwoo industry, indicating a spread across various industries [40, 51, 57, 58, 62]. Gyeonggi Province is scheduled to host the 'International Forum on Clean Air' on the 27th to discuss climate crisis response, and Yeosu City is strengthening policy support by increasing its supplementary budget by 10.7 billion KRW for carbon neutrality and urban environmental improvement [4, 20, 32, 63, 70].

sections.title: ⚡️ Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating both domestically and internationally, but complexities arising from increased electricity demand and supply shortages are being raised. Minister of Climate Kim Sung-hwan proposed that a mix of nuclear power, centered on renewable energy, is necessary for AI operations, and the required renewable energy supply of 100GW for the three mega-projects by 2030 is insufficient, expected to meet only 58% of electricity demand even upon target achievement [76, 77, 91, 101]. Domestically, the renewable energy supply outlook for the 12th Basic Plan for Long-term Electricity Supply and Demand (Electricity Basic Plan) is scheduled to be released next week, and discussions will cover the scale of solar and wind power deployment by 2040 and the establishment of innovative expansion strategies [79, 94, 97, 98, 99]. KORAIL is demonstrating public sector efforts towards renewable energy transition by expanding solar power generation to 117 GWh using idle railway spaces and directly purchasing the generated electricity [83, 84, 96, 102]. Furthermore, the Saemangeum development plan includes Hyundai Motor Group's investment, along with AI data centers, solar power, and hydrogen production facilities, and private sector participation is also active, with Naver investing in renewable energy power plants in preparation for a threefold increase in electricity consumption [105, 108]. In Latin America and the Caribbean, 64% of electricity generated in May came from renewable sources, but warnings have also emerged that climate change is testing the resilience of renewable energy [78, 117].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Change Awareness and Response Efforts
sections.content: The international community is raising awareness of climate change and exploring various response measures. Angola's peatlands have been confirmed to be four times larger than previously thought, revealing their potential role in slowing climate change [110]. Discussions are underway regarding the risks of geoengineering the atmosphere to combat climate change and who should make such decisions, with the importance of land use for clean energy transition also being emphasized [113, 120]. Conversely, concerning movements have been observed in the education sector, such as the quiet removal of climate change-related content from textbooks in Florida [112]. Youth in Arizona are demanding action on extreme heat and climate change, and a letter has been published advocating for climate change to be a central issue in election campaigns, indicating a growing voice from civil society [111, 118, 125, 126]. London is projected to incur costs of up to 36 billion pounds annually by the 2050s due to climate change, and a report highlighting the mental health costs of climate change has also been released, indicating a growing awareness of its widespread impacts [119, 127].

briefing.closing: Today's climate-related news once again reminds us that the global climate crisis is deepening, while simultaneously demonstrating active adaptation and mitigation efforts across various sectors to overcome it. This concludes the climate briefing for August 20, 2026.
